title: Tue 3 Nov: Nifty's third straight gain meets election-day jitters
description:
Hot topic: the Nifty jumped 1.7% for a third straight gain on Reliance's record profit and a Brent slump, but a Korean chip sell-off and US election day point to a flat start. Then: Reliance, oil, SBI, ITC, Infosys, the US midterms, the rupee, Dixon and IndiGo.

1. Nifty jumps 1.7% to 23,441 for a third straight gain as Reliance soars 11.6% (HDFC Sky / IIFL Securities)
2. Reliance's record 29,550 crore rupee profit sends the stock up 11.6% (HDFC Sky / IIFL Securities)
3. Brent falls 7.6% to 104.77 dollars as Iran peace-talk hopes grow (Nation Thailand / Reuters)
4. SBI reports Q2 today; analysts see profit from flat to up 25% (Business Standard / Trade Brains)
5. ITC's Q2 profit falls 20% to 4,137 crore rupees, in line with estimates (IndiaIPO / Upstox)
6. Infosys goes ex-dividend for its 26 rupee interim payout (TradingView / Moody's; Yahoo Finance)
7. Americans vote in the midterms with the 10-year Treasury yield near 4.89% (Yahoo Finance / Bloomberg; StockTitan)
8. Rupee slips 10 paise to 94.86 despite cheaper oil (HDFC Sky / PTI)
9. Dixon soars 12% as 47% revenue growth outweighs a 45% profit fall (Kotak Neo)
10. IndiGo trails the rally even as Brent slides (Yahoo Finance / Nation Thailand)

From the Ripple news desk. Voices are AI-generated with open-source Kokoro voices. This is news, not investment advice; the hosts are not SEBI-registered advisers.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Good morning, this is Ripple Daily. I'm P.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: And I'm S. Ten stories, under ten minutes.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Today's big one: the Nifty's third straight gain runs into weak chip stocks, on US election day.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: S, start with Monday. What happened?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: A big rally. The Nifty closed at 23,440.80, up 387.70 points or 1.68%. The Sensex rose 1.66% to 75,692.78.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Was it broad, or just a few names?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Broad. 2,668 NSE stocks rose and 1,469 fell. But Reliance did the heavy lifting, jumping 11.6% on a record profit.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Who else moved?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Oil helped. Brent then settled 7.6% lower at 104.77 dollars, on hopes of Iran peace talks. Infosys and IT lagged as the Nasdaq slipped.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Okay, one stock and one commodity. Is that a real rally?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Now, why it matters. A rally led by one heavyweight and cheaper oil is fragile, and global tech cues turned weak overnight.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The Nasdaq fell 1.1%, and Korea's Kospi opened 3.6% lower on chip selling. GIFT Nifty points to a flat start near 23,400.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: So what's the trigger to watch?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Whether the Nifty holds 23,300 despite weak Asian chips. A deep tech sell-off that drags it back below 23,200 would undo the move.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: And the stocks?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Stocks in focus: Reliance, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Infosys. Sentiment: mixed.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Rapid fire. Story two: Reliance posts a record profit, and the stock flies.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: September-quarter profit rose 40.6% to a record 29,550 crore rupees, led by a 68% jump in refining earnings. The stock closed up 11.6%.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Any weak spot?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Retail profit fell 24.3%. And Brent's further fall trims the windfall-margin case, though brokerages stayed positive.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: after a move several times its normal range, day two shows whether funds keep chasing it. Sentiment: positive. Stocks in focus: Reliance, IOC, BPCL, Hindustan Petroleum.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story three: oil drops below 105 dollars on peace-talk hopes.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Brent settled at 104.77 dollars, down 8.66 dollars or 7.6%. WTI fell 7.4% to 96.46, its first close below 100 dollars in weeks.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: What changed?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Iran's president said the Supreme Leader gave his government authority for peace talks, and President Trump said a deal could happen.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Analysts at Raymond James and UBS warned of earlier false dawns, and prices stay very sensitive to Middle East headlines.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: cheaper oil eases India's import bill, inflation and the rupee. Sentiment: positive. Stocks in focus: BPCL, IOC, IndiGo, ONGC.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story four: SBI reports results today. What's the range?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Wide. Brokerages see profit anywhere from flat, at Kotak, to about 25% growth, at Motilal Oswal. Net interest income is seen up 11 to 13%.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Anything that could flatter the number?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: One-off gains from stake sales in SBI Funds and NSE. And Bank of Baroda's 36% profit jump last week set a high bar.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: SBI is the largest PSU-bank weight, so its margins and asset quality set the group's tone. Sentiment: neutral. Stocks in focus: SBI, Bank of Baroda, BSE.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story five: ITC's profit falls 20%. Was that a shock?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: No, it was close to estimates. Net profit fell 20.1% to 4,137 crore rupees, while revenue excluding excise rose 1.8% to 18,401 crore.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Where's the pain?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Margins. EBITDA fell 17.5%, and margins dropped 660 basis points to 28%. The stock closed near 264.55 rupees, close to its 52-week low.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: an in-line print tests whether the cigarette-tax shock is fully priced in. Sentiment: mixed. Stocks in focus: ITC, Hindustan Unilever, Godfrey Phillips.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story six: Infosys goes ex-dividend today. Expect a dip?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Mechanically, yes. Today is the record date for its 26 rupee interim dividend, so the price should drop by about 26 rupees, roughly 2.2%.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Anything else weighing on it?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: It closed Monday at 1,161 rupees, down 2%. Overnight the Nasdaq fell another 1.1% and Nvidia slipped 1.3%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: a mechanical drop meets weak global tech cues for India's second-largest IT stock. Sentiment: negative. Stocks in focus: Infosys, TCS, HCLTech.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story seven: America votes in the midterms today. Why should India care?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Results come after the US close. The 10-year Treasury yield ended Monday near 4.89%, down about 3.5 basis points, its lowest since 10 September.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: What comes after the vote?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The October jobs report on Friday, with economists expecting about 55,000 new jobs.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: the result shapes the US fiscal path and long-term yields, which drive global capital flows to India. Sentiment: neutral.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story eight: the rupee slipped, even with oil falling.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The rupee closed at a provisional 94.86 per dollar, 10 paise weaker, even as Brent fell and Indian stocks rallied.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Why didn't it gain?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: It suggests the RBI is holding the pair in a tight range. Brent's slide and a softer dollar index near 101.8 now support the rupee.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: oil is India's biggest import, so a 9 dollar fall in Brent is the rupee's strongest support in weeks. Sentiment: mixed.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story nine: Dixon's profit falls 45%, and the stock jumps 12%. Explain.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Revenue rose 47%, and investors cared more about that than the fall in profit, to 411 crore rupees. The stock closed at 12,319 rupees.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Will it hold?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The test is Korea. Samsung and SK Hynix fell about 5% overnight in a chip and electronics sell-off.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: Dixon is a bellwether for India's electronics push, testing appetite for growth over margins. Sentiment: mixed. Stocks in focus: Dixon, Kaynes, Amber Enterprises.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Last one. Story ten: IndiGo lags, despite cheaper oil.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: IndiGo closed Monday at 4,919.90 rupees, up 0.9%, behind the Nifty's 1.7% gain. It had jumped 4.3% on Friday on a narrower quarterly loss.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: And oil since then?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Brent fell a further 3.5% after the Indian close, extending the fuel-cost relief.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: fuel is about a third of an airline's costs, so oil moves feed straight into margins. Sentiment: positive. Stocks in focus: IndiGo.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: What to watch today: SBI's results, whether the Nifty holds 23,300, and the US vote count tonight.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: That's Ripple Daily. Full stories and sources are in the show notes. This is news, not investment advice. We're not SEBI-registered advisers.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: See you tomorrow morning.
